awd_titl_txt: Conference: 24th Annual Symposium of the NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellows
awd_abstract_narration:
This award will provide support for the attendees and invited speakers for the twenty fourth Annual Symposium of the NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellows, to be held in conjunction with the winter meeting of the American Astronomical Society in January 2026, in Phoenix, AZ. The purpose of the Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellowships (AAPF) Program is to support integrated research and education activities at the postdoctoral level to better prepare its fellows for positions of distinction and leadership in the scientific community. The Annual Symposium provides a forum for the Fellows to discuss their research and education projects while increasing their visibility within the astronomy and astrophysics community. The Symposium represents a key component of the AAPF Program and is a very effective mechanism to facilitate the transfer of knowledge and experience that the Fellows have acquired through their postdoctoral training.

As with previous symposia in this series, the 2026 AAPF Symposium will promote interactions among astronomers with diverse research interests and backgrounds. By creating a forum in which discussions can occur across traditional research boundaries, the Symposium will provide Fellows the opportunity to gain new insights and pursue interdisciplinary collaborations. The Symposium will also provide a venue for discussing major issues that are important to early-career astronomers. In addition, the Symposium will (1) provide a forum to discuss integrated research and education activities, (2) facilitate collaborations between Fellows on both research and education, and (3) provide greater exposure for the Fellows and the AAPF Program within the astronomical community.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Project Outcomes Report: NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Symposium

The 2026 NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Symposium successfully brought together postdoctoral fellows from across the United States for two days of scientific exchange, professional development, and community building. The symposium was conceived and organized to strengthen the intellectual and collaborative connections among fellows funded through the NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellowships (AAPF) and the Mathematical and Physical Sciences Ascend Postdoctoral Fellowship programs.

Overview and Participation

A total of 28 NSF postdoctoral fellows attended the symposium, representing a broad range of research areas across astrophysics, cosmology, and instrumentation. Attendance was balanced across first-, second-, and third-year fellows (approximately 32%, 36%, and 32% of participants, respectively), ensuring a strong mix of experience levels and perspectives. The meeting featured 33 fellow presentations that highlighted both scientific research and broader impact projects, ranging from cutting-edge results on sophisticated instrumentation and stellar populations to innovative outreach and mentoring initiatives.

Program Highlights

The symposium included two keynote presentations and two professional development sessions designed to promote both scientific and societal impact:

  • Science Keynote: Dr. Roohi Dalal, Deputy Director of Public Policy for the AAS, gave a presentation on how the current fellows can better engage with the AAS and wider astronomy community on the national and local level.

  • Broader Impacts Keynote: Dra. Nicole Cabrera-Salazar, founder of Movement Consulting, shared strategies for building inclusive pathways for all students in physics and astronomy.

  • Finance Workshop: Dr. Jonathan Fox & Dr. Suzanne Bartholomae, professors in finance and economics from Iowa State University, led a hands-on session on financial well-being to help build good practices in personal finances.

  • Mentorship Workshop: Prof. Mia de los Reyes, professor of astronomy from UMass Amherst, led a workshop on what it means to successfully mentor a summer research student by setting strategic goals for the mentor and mentee(s), designing projects (both in terms of content and logistics) that can meet those goals, and developing structures to maintain healthy mentoring relationships throughout and beyond the summer.

Intellectual Merit

The symposium advanced the intellectual goals of the NSF postdoctoral programs by fostering collaboration across subfields of astronomy and astrophysics. Fellows exchanged insights on methodologies, data analysis techniques, and emerging research directions in areas such as stellar evolution, galaxy formation, and time-domain astrophysics. Informal networking and structured discussion sessions led to new collaborative ideas and follow-up research plans among participants.

Broader Impacts

Beyond scientific exchange, the symposium strengthened the fellows’ collective capacity to engage in education, outreach, and mentoring. Sessions on storytelling, inclusive program development, and career navigation helped attendees translate their scientific expertise into public communication and community engagement. The event also provided fellows—many of whom are early in their independent research careers—with valuable professional development resources and a sense of community that will support their transition to leadership roles in academia and beyond.

Post-symposium survey results indicate majority positive responses, with 3 of the 4 invited speaker sessions rated between 4 and 5 (on a 0–5 scale) for usefulness and overall satisfaction. Attendees emphasized that the symposium provided unique opportunities for connection and mentorship not available through virtual or program-specific meetings. They also found that the sessions on mentoring were particularly valuable for developing pedagogical approaches and outreach strategies.

Documentation and Legacy

A dedicated website page was created to host the symposium schedule, presentation summaries, and photo highlights. This resource will remain available to future cohorts of NSF postdoctoral fellows as a model for effective scientific and professional networking.

In summary, this symposium achieved its central goals: it promoted collaboration, professional development, and community among the next generation of astrophysicists, while showcasing the excellence of NSF-supported research. The overwhelmingly positive feedback underscores its value as a model for future gatherings of NSF postdoctoral fellows.
